initial_hypotheses: payment-service POST /charge spans pin at ~3000ms without errors, indicating a resource wait (connection pool/queue/lock) rather than compute; its redis/postgres dependencies are candidate stall points
order-service POST /checkout returns 502 after ~2000ms while calling payment-service, suggesting a downstream timeout or gRPC/HTTP deadline breach propagating upstream to gateway
gateway 502s are secondary propagation from order-service, not an independent gateway fault, since gateway user-service/redis paths show no latency anomaly
shared redis/postgres runtime pool saturation across order-service and payment-service could serialize requests and produce the near-fixed 2s/3s latency plateaus

arguments.hypothesis: payment-service POST /charge exhibits a near-constant ~3009ms self-blocking latency (p50 3006 / p95 3007 plateau) with HTTP 200, while order-service POST /checkout fails 502 at ~2020ms and gateway propagates that 502. The fixed ~3s plateau in payment is the origin of the checkout failures; order-service/gateway are downstream-derived symptoms. Candidate mechanism: a fixed-wait resource (connection pool wait / scheduled delay / lock) in payment-service, not compute.
arguments.reasoning_summary: Trace dbf1e653 shows payment POST /charge = 3009ms (no error) as the deepest long span, with order POST /checkout 2019ms/502 and gateway POST /checkout 2022ms/502 as ancestors. Metrics show payment p50~3007 vs p95~3010 (tight plateau) and order-service error_pct 100% in the fresh window while payment error_pct 0. Pool stats show payment usage_ms 30859, requests_wait_ms 3204 — but requests_waiting 0, so pool exhaustion not confirmed yet.
arguments.next_evidence_needed: Read full payment POST /charge span children (trace detail beyond truncation) and source for charge/pricing path to identify the concrete ~3s stall (fixed sleep vs downstream call vs lock). Also check redis TTL evidence E-86474f8236c64d97 and DB evidence E-1ac53f60851d4adc/E-e6596e4174174258.
